chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Al-Husayn al-Ahmasi from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir and Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about vinegar being added to wine, he said: 'Not except what comes from itself (i.e., natural transformation), so it does not contradict the earlier reports, because the matter is to be understood as a type of dislike, for it is preferable to leave it until it becomes vinegar naturally.'

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَة: Dislike (a legal status between permissibility and prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on adding vinegar to wine to make it permissible?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on wine turned to vinegar (*khamr al-khall*), distinguishing between vinegar formed by human intervention (adding vinegar) and that formed naturally. He notes that while adding vinegar does not contradict earlier reports, it is preferable (*afdal*) to let the transformation occur naturally to avoid the subtle impurity or *karahah* associated with artificial conversion. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of preferring natural processes in purification to ensure the substance is fully distinct from its original state of intoxication.
